taxonomy.subtopic: Renal ammoniagenesis and new bicarbonate generation

questions.stem_html: A 63-year-old man with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is clinically stable. Arterial blood gas analysis shows pH 7.36, PCO2 60 mm Hg, and HCO3− 33 mEq/L. The accompanying graph shows the expected bicarbonate response to sustained hypercapnia. Which renal adaptation is most important for producing this pattern?

options.text_html: Increased chloride reabsorption in exchange for bicarbonate secretion by type B intercalated cells
Increased proximal-tubule glutamine metabolism with greater NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> excretion and generation of new bicarbonate
Reduced proximal bicarbonate reabsorption caused by inhibition of carbonic anhydrase
Decreased distal hydrogen secretion with increased urinary bicarbonate loss
Immediate buffering of hydrogen ions by intracellular proteins without a change in renal acid excretion

questions.explanation_html: Chronic hypercapnia lowers the bicarbonate-to-PCO2 ratio. Over several days, the kidneys increase net acid excretion, especially as ammonium generated from proximal-tubule glutamine metabolism, and increase bicarbonate reabsorption and new bicarbonate generation. This raises plasma bicarbonate and moves pH toward normal without fully correcting the primary respiratory disorder.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Chronic respiratory acidosis increases, rather than decreases, renal hydrogen secretion and bicarbonate conservation.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Nonbicarbonate buffering contributes to the small acute rise in bicarbonate but cannot explain the larger chronic renal compensation.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Reduced bicarbonate reabsorption would worsen acidemia.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Type B intercalated cells secrete bicarbonate during alkalosis; chronic respiratory acidosis favors acid secretion by type A intercalated cells.

questions.educational_objective: Renal compensation for chronic respiratory acidosis requires increased ammonium excretion, titratable acid excretion, bicarbonate reabsorption, and new bicarbonate generation.
